name: MO-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's 21-point Republican partisan lean anchors the seat firmly on the GOP side
Alford's roughly 33-to-1 fundraising advantage over Herrera ($1.39M vs $42K)
Prediction markets price the Democrat at only about 3%
No polls or expert ratings; a Libertarian on the ballot may trim Alford's share slightly
model.rationale: The district's 21-point Republican lean, Alford's overwhelming financial edge, and markets pricing the Democrat near 3% all point to a comfortable incumbent hold; with no polls or ratings signaling competition, only the size of the margin is in question.
model.watch: A late scandal or a wave of outside spending against Alford could narrow the margin, though the seat's lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Missouri's 4th District sits deep in Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly 21 points toward the GOP. Mark Alford, the incumbent, is running for re-election after securing renomination. His campaign has raised about $1.39 million and holds roughly $747,000 on hand, while Democratic nominee Jordan Herrera has raised about $42,000 with under $20,000 available. A Libertarian candidate, Thomas Holbrook, also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give the Democrat about a 3% chance of winning. The combination of the district's strong lean, Alford's incumbency and financial dominance, and the challenger's minimal resources makes this a safe Republican seat. The main uncertainty is the size of the margin rather than the outcome, with the third-party candidate potentially trimming Alford's total slightly.
